title: Owner decisions needed
body:
@MichaelZelbel, 26 owner-only decisions are open (manager pass 2026-11-23 10:45 UTC: **added** four: one more lap for two approved, parked pull requests (PR #1029, PR #1038), and three the loop parked for you: what the chat says when asked for a brief on a morning with none saved (#1070), a time of day on moments (#1059), and date ranges on records other than moments (#1060). Nothing was answered or defaulted since 07:45 UTC. Earlier passes: see the comments below).

**The answers that would unblock the most:** (1) the merge-gate fault, which still costs about one lap in three; (2) one more lap each for PR #895 (#887, the layout check that would catch the long-name defects that keep coming back), PR #990 and PR #953; (3) the OpenRouter key, without which no AI scenario or release can be proven until 2026-12-01.

### The empty Recent People card still shows a heart (look and feel)
#964 removed "cherishing" from the empty Recent People card. Its review noticed that the small heart icon before "No one here yet. Add your first person." is still there, a leftover of the old skin's look.
Options: (a) keep the heart; (b) use the same people icon as the card's header, or none. Recommendation: (b). Default after 2026-11-24 10:15 UTC: wait; this is how the Dashboard looks.

### Fix the release step that opened a lower version (#726)
At 14:46 UTC the release step opened #725, which would have set main's version from 2.0.0-beta.28 back to 2.0.0-beta.27 and was set to merge itself once `required` passed. The manager closed it. The release step has no source in this repository, so the loop cannot fix it.
Options: fix the release step where it lives (it should refuse any version at or below the base branch's), or move #726 to that repository. Recommendation: fix it there and close #726 with a link. Default after 2026-11-20 15:00 UTC: wait; that automation is outside the loop's reach.

### Raise or replace the scenarios' OpenRouter key (monthly limit reached)
The candidate proof for 2.0.0-beta.28 (run 44317302991, 14:20 UTC) failed 11 scenarios. The ones checked fail with `HTTP 403: Key limit exceeded (monthly limit)` from OpenRouter for the scenario key, not on the product. Until the key works, every AI scenario in the nightly and candidate runs fails for this reason, and no release can be proven.
Options: raise the key's monthly limit, or put a new key in the `GODSPEED_SCENARIO_AI_KEY` secret. Recommendation: raise the limit. Default after 2026-11-20 15:00 UTC: wait; spending and secrets are yours.
Update 2026-11-19: the key is at $15.00 of $15.00 and resets 2026-12-01 (loop review of PR #749). #762 (filed this pass) found that an open notebook page with a connected AI sends it a billed test question every 5 seconds; scenario runs that leave a page open may be what spends this key.


Update 2026-11-21 07:15 UTC: priority #721 (the lost Night chat tidy-up) is now parked on this too. (Update 15:45 UTC: no longer; #721 is closed, its scenario passed on main c8e189660 in run 44908086448.) PR #749 merged the evidence, and naming the gate that drops the job needs one scenario run that the AI can answer.
### Identify or expose the owner-question gateway (#600)
The maintained renderer/parser is outside this repository in a separate root-owned Hermes gateway.
Options: grant isolated read-only access, identify the external repository/service and move #600, or close it as outside scope. Recommendation: move it to the maintained owner. Default after 2026-11-18 13:30 UTC: wait; access and external scope are owner decisions.

### Download the food table only when the food tracker is used?
Every fresh notebook downloads the BLS food table from `www.blsdb.de` about 60 seconds after it starts (`notebook/server/main.mjs`, `foodTableWanted`). This happens even for people who never use the food tracker, so every new notebook contacts a third party unasked. #731 stopped chat messages from reaching food hosts and left this startup download to you (its review's "Noticed" section).
Options: keep the startup download (the table is ready offline at once), or download it the first time the person uses food tracking or names a food (no third-party contact until then; the first lookup waits for the download). Recommendation: download on first use. Default after 2026-11-20 18:35 UTC: wait; this is product behaviour and yours to decide.

### Should a newly watched domain that is already free send a notice? (#745)
Your #706 ticket asks for one notice per change of state. It does not say whether the first reading counts. Today, if the person starts watching a domain that can already be registered, they are never told.
Options: send one "free now" notice on the first reading when the domain is already available (and nothing for other first states); or keep first readings silent. Recommendation: send it, since being told a wanted name is free is the point of the watch. Default after 2026-11-20 21:00 UTC: wait; this is product behaviour.

### Public verification routes for the talk journeys (#616)
PR #618 now continues under your beta.29 ticket for #670 (installed talk preparation), so its lap question is answered. What #616 asked for beyond that is still open: maintained routes that let the talk-preparation journeys be checked end to end on a normal install (the holdout runs still cannot reach a verdict on four of them, tracked on #616).
Options: fold it into a later release plan item; or close #616 once #670 merges and see what is still unreachable then. Recommendation: wait for #670 to merge, then the manager rechecks and narrows #616 to what remains. Default after 2026-11-20 21:00 UTC: wait; scope is yours.

### Free-text evidence for a Godspeed-owned file result (#748)
Today `mc-work verify <id> --evidence "..."` marks a Godspeed-owned file result verified on any free text, without the content review against its DONE WHEN that #710 adds. No shipped recipe uses that path unattended, but an assistant that adds `--evidence` itself could report a shape-only draft as ready in the morning message.
Options: (a) keep it as is (evidence is for what a person observed); (b) require the content review as well whenever the result is Godspeed-owned; (c) accept `--evidence` only when it carries the person's own words (for example given through a waiting step), not the assistant's. Recommendation: (b), so nothing Godspeed made is called verified without the review. Default after 2026-11-21 00:30 UTC: wait; this is product behaviour.

### The loop's land step merges before CI finishes (loop fault, outside this repository)
Since 00:30 UTC, `gh pr merge` refused 9 approved merges: #765 four times, #710 twice, and #708, #750 and #768 once each. Each time the reviewer had merged main into the branch and called `gh pr merge` within seconds, before CI and `required` had finished on the new head, so "the base branch policy prohibits the merge". Each refusal costs a full lap, and #765 and #710 were parked at the cap for it (the manager merged #765 at its reviewed head once `required` passed). The land step lives in the pinned Archon workflow (`factory/pack.json`), which the loop may not change.
Options: (a) change the land step to wait for `required` on the exact head before merging (or to use `gh pr merge --auto --match-head-commit`); (b) keep it as is. Recommendation: (a). Default after 2026-11-21 03:20 UTC: wait, because the workflow is outside the loop's reach.

Update 2026-11-19 06:10 UTC: a second form of the same fault. The gate now also refuses an approved head with "the commit to merge is not what the app check tested", after the reviewer has merged main into the branch. For #771 and #767 the manager checked this: the diff from the app-checked commit to the head was byte-for-byte the diff main itself made, so both heads were clean merges and the refusals were wrong. Each was parked by the dispatcher for it. The manager merged both at their reviewed heads with `--match-head-commit`, once `required` had passed. Option (a) above would prevent both forms: let the gate accept a head whose difference from the tested commit is only main's own change, or stop the reviewer from merging main after the app check unless GitHub reports a conflict.

Update 2026-11-19 09:20 UTC: 5 more refusals since 06:25 (#786 twice, #781, #794 and #799). Both refusals of #786 were "repository rule violations" on a freshly merged head whose CI had not finished. #781 was refused as "not mergeable". #799 was refused because main had moved and now conflicts. #794 was also refused for H-47, H-49 and H-50 as "untracked", although #796 had fixed them on main eight minutes earlier.

Update 2026-11-19 12:30 UTC: 13 more refusals since 09:29 (#817, #815 twice, #814 twice, #810 three times, #802 twice, #799 twice, #797), against 5 merges. Most are "the commit to merge is not what the app check tested" after main moved, or "base branch policy prohibits the merge" on a head whose `required` had not finished. With main moving every 20-30 minutes, most approved pull requests now need two or three laps to land.

Update 2026-11-21 04:20 UTC: since launches resumed (01:18 UTC) the gate refused 6 more approved merges between 03:02 and 03:57 (#857 twice, #835, #858, #828, #860), each a lap. The land step now also merges "outside the merge gate" when the gate refuses (#856, #835, #857); `required` still had to pass, so nothing unreviewed landed, but it shows the gate's refusals are the problem, not the work.

Update 2026-11-21 10:15 UTC: 3 more refusals since 07:15 (#872, #880 and #883 at 10:01, "Required status check \"required\" is expected"), against 4 merges. #880 and #883 still landed on later laps. The manager merged #872 after checking that main merged into its reviewed head still passed the layout audit.

Update 2026-11-22 22:20 UTC: 13 more refusals between 19:43 and 22:07 UTC (#983, #985, #994, #995, #990 and #980 twice each, #992 once), against 5 merges. Every one was "not mergeable", "Required status check \"required\" is expected", "still a draft" or "not what the app check tested" right after the reviewer pushed a merge of main. Four of them parked approved work at the cap; the manager verified and merged those four (#983, #985, #994, #995). This fault now costs about half of all laps.

Update 2026-11-23 04:45 UTC: 5 more refusals since 02:05 UTC (#1030 twice, #1029, #1031, #1036), against 4 loop merges, none on the work. The manager landed #1024 itself (three clean main-merges, rebuilt with `git merge-tree`). #1029 could not be landed that way: main changed one of its files after the check.

### Run the default-wait check on notebook-only changes (#789 / PR #797)
The manager approved PR #797's new check (it fails any UI or notebook test that waits with the library's default limit) and its shared wait limits (Manager decision on #789). One step is left that only you can make, because builders may not edit CI workflows. The check runs only from `.github/workflows/notebook-ui.yml`, and that workflow skips pull requests that change only `notebook/test/**`. The change is one line, made twice (the pull_request and push `paths`):
```diff
-    paths: ['notebook/ui/**', '.github/workflows/notebook-ui.yml']
+    paths: ['notebook/ui/**', 'notebook/test/**', '.github/workflows/notebook-ui.yml']
```
Options: (a) add it; (b) leave it out. Without it, a notebook-only PR that adds a default wait merges green, and the next UI PR (or the manager's pass) turns red on it. Recommendation: (a). Default after 2026-11-21 09:20 UTC: wait; CI workflows are protected.

### The nightly run proves a commit whose server image does not exist yet (#820)
The nightly run started at 10:35 UTC on 93072fa2d, one minute after it merged. Its server image was published at 11:00, so the stage job stopped ("No server image ... exists") and no scenario ran. Main now moves every 20-30 minutes, so a night can miss like this again whenever a merge lands shortly before the schedule. The fix is in `.github/workflows/scenarios.yml`, which the loop may not change.
Options: (a) have the nightly prove the newest main commit that already has an image; (b) have it wait (up to about 40 minutes) for the image of its commit; (c) leave it, and accept a missed night now and then. Recommendation: (a). Default after 2026-11-21 12:30 UTC: wait; CI workflows are protected. (Until 2026-12-01 the AI scenarios also fail on the scenario key's monthly limit, above.)

Update 2026-11-21 10:15 UTC: it happened again tonight. The night of 2026-11-21 started on d3592eeb6, 9 minutes after it merged, before its image existed, so no scenario ran (#820).

### One land-only lap for three more parked, approved pull requests (#958 / PR #990, #950 / PR #953)
(Update 2026-11-22 19:20 UTC: #814 merged at 18:05 UTC under your beta.30 decision on #805; only #802 remains here.)
(Update 2026-11-22 10:15 UTC: #815 merged at 07:38 UTC; #814 and #802 remain.)
(Update 2026-11-22 01:15 UTC: for #815, Mission Control merged main into the branch at 00:00 UTC (656e1d06c) and will land it after the beta.29 release is on the server, so #815 no longer needs your answer here. #814 (priority #805) and #802 still do.)
(Update 2026-11-21 19:15 UTC: #810 is closed; its issue #803 was delivered by #866.)
Each was approved by every loop review and refused only by the merge gate's timing fault (above), and each is now past the loop's attempt limit, so the manager gives them no more laps. Main has moved since, so none can be merged at its reviewed head: #815 and #810 still merge cleanly with main 65150708e, and #814 and #802 now conflict. (The same applies to #799, #773, #754 and #710, already above.)
Options: (a) authorize one land-only lap each: merge main, re-run the app check, land only once `required` is green on that exact head; (b) close them and let new laps rebuild what is still missing; (c) leave them parked. Recommendation: (a), after the merge-gate fault above is fixed, or each lap risks another refusal. Default after 2026-11-23 01:45 UTC: wait; the lap budget is yours.

Update 2026-11-21 04:20 UTC: #815 and #810 are still cleanly mergeable with `required` green on their heads; #814 and #802 conflict. #814 is the fix for #805 (priority: the notebook does not start when its saved AI connection file is damaged; the review of PR #830 saw it again on main today), so it matters most of the four. #806, the one-AI-state fix that covers #803's case, no longer waits for #810 (manager comment on #806), so a lap can build it either way.


Update 2026-11-21 07:15 UTC: these parked pull requests are now most of what holds the loop. #815 and #810 still merge cleanly with `required` green on their heads, and #814 (priority #805) and #802 conflict. The manager did not merge #815 or #810 at their old reviewed heads, because main has changed the same AI-failure code many times since 2026-11-19, so the merged result would be untested.
Update 2026-11-22 22:20 UTC: three more items are past the attempt limit, each with its blocker named. #958 / PR #990 (search keeps taking in notes after the folder changes): approved twice; the gate refused it because the app check carried a result from a commit that is not an ancestor of the head, so it needs a fresh app check on its head, then land. #959 / PR #962 (no Sign Out on a local notebook): the app check passed C1-C3; four new tests use the default wait limit that the suite's guard refuses, so it needs only `WAIT` passed to those calls. #950 / PR #953 (a write filter that cannot pick a record is refused): the manager recorded on #950 how the filter must learn each kind's fields; it needs one lap to build that. #956 waits on #950. Recommendation: (a), one lap each. Default after 2026-11-25 00:00 UTC: wait; the lap budget is yours.

Update 2026-11-23 04:45 UTC: your beta.31 tickets settle #802 (ticket 03 on #784) and #959 / PR #962 (ticket 08), so only #958 / PR #990 and #950 / PR #953 are still asked here.

### Where Settings shows "Import from Menerio" (look and feel)
On a fresh notebook, the first and most prominent thing in Settings is a filled blue "Import from Menerio" button, above "Your AI", which is the one thing a new person has to set up there. Most people have no Menerio notebook to import.
Options: (a) keep it where it is; (b) move it into a smaller "Bring in notes from elsewhere" line below Your AI (or into the Import/Export part of Settings); (c) show it only when a Menerio account or export is detected. Recommendation: (b). Default after 2026-11-23 01:45 UTC: wait; this is how the notebook looks.




### Search after a note is overwritten from outside without its frontmatter (#932)
A note made in the app, then rewritten from outside (another editor or a sync tool) as plain text with no frontmatter, never reaches search again: its new text is not found for at least 30 s, on main and on the branches tested. The notebook cannot tell a stripped note from a stranger's file.
Options: (a) keep it: the file has lost its identity, and the note stays as it was until the 10-minute store check; say so in the guide; (b) take the new text into the same note, so search finds it within seconds, as for any other outside edit; (c) refuse the file and keep the original note, telling the person. Recommendation: (b): an editor that drops frontmatter is a normal way to edit notes from outside, and the person expects the new text to be found. Default after 2026-11-24 01:15 UTC: wait; this is what a person gets.

Update 2026-11-23 01:35 UTC: 9 more refusals since 23:08 (#1002 and #1010 twice each, #1013, #1027, #1009, #1024, #1006), against 6 loop merges. Seven were "not what the app check tested (it changed more than a clean merge)". The manager read the pinned gate (`.archon/workflows/sdlc/.shared/merge-gate.ts`, `untestedMerge`). It accepts the head only when the head tree equals *the tested commit merged with the default branch as it is now*. So a reviewer who merged main into the branch even once, if main has moved since or the reviewer fetched an older main, is always refused, however clean the merges were. #1010 is an example: three clean merges of main, none touching its two files. A fix that keeps the protection: compare the head with the tested commit merged with **the main commit the head actually contains** (the head's newest first-parent merge of main), and keep the check that none of those main commits touches a file of the change. The manager checked and landed three such approved pull requests itself this pass (#1010, #1003, #1002).

### One more lap for PR #895 (#887, priority), over the merge-gate cap
PR #895 makes the page-wide layout check open every page filled, at four widths, on every tab (the fix for the class behind #863, #867, #868, #871 and #878). The merge gate refused it twice (22:40 and 00:06 UTC), both times because the reviewer merged a moving main after the app check, not for the code. The manager recorded the review's D1 as settled by #930 (Manager decision on #895). It now conflicts with main.
Options: (a) one lap to merge main, re-run the app check and land at the tested head; (b) close it and rebuild #887 from main. Recommendation: (a), ideally after the merge-gate fault above is fixed. Default after 2026-11-24 01:15 UTC: wait; the lap budget is yours.

Update 2026-11-22 22:20 UTC: six more defects of exactly the kind #887 would catch reached main or review since this question was asked: #987, #996, #997, #998, #1004 and #1005 (long names and words cut off, overflowing, or squeezed at phone widths). Each costs its own issue and lap. This lap is now the one that saves the most later laps.

### The My Profile dot is red on every fresh notebook (look and feel)
#985 gave the dot beside My Profile a tooltip ("Profile 0% complete") and kept its colour, as its criterion said. On a fresh notebook it is red (the error colour) from the first minute, so it still reads as something wrong before the person has done anything (manager pass 2026-11-22 22:20 UTC).
Options: (a) keep red below 30%; (b) a neutral or blue colour for an unfilled profile, with red kept for nothing; (c) no dot until the person has started their profile. Recommendation: (b). Default after 2026-11-25 00:00 UTC: wait; this is how the notebook looks.

### How an open collection item should lay out on a phone (#1005 / PR #1008, over the send-back cap)
PR #1008 hides the item list when an item is open at phone widths. That fixes the 50 px strip. Its second send-back found that the pinned footer (Delete, Back, Save), once it wraps, leaves the item's fields in a nested scroll area 180 px tall at 320x640, under the contract's 200 px minimum. Each fix moved the problem somewhere else, so the loop parked it at the cap.
Options: (a) on phones the whole page scrolls, with no nested area and the footer at the end of the fields; (b) keep the footer pinned and accept a shorter field area at 320x640. Recommendation: (a). Every field stays reachable and it matches how #1006 settled the person page. Default after 2026-11-25 01:30 UTC: wait; this is how the notebook looks. Once you answer, one more lap builds it.

### Should the person page's header card stay pinned on phones? (#1011, look and feel)
Since #1006, below 640 px the person page's header card scrolls away with the page, so a very long name can be read. Before that it stayed in view.
Options: (a) keep it scrolling with the page; (b) pin a compact bar (name plus Edit and Merge) on phones; (c) pin the full card only when it is shorter than a third of the screen. Recommendation: (b). The person's name and actions stay in reach, and a long name is still readable in the card above. Default after 2026-11-25 01:30 UTC: wait; this is how the notebook looks. (The separate defect in landscape, a 100 px scroll strip, is #1033 and does not wait on this.)

### Should a group's Add Members dialog let you add a new person? (#1041, scope)
In People > Groups > a group > Add Members, the dialog lists only people already in the notebook. People, the header's quick add and a moment's People picker all let you create a new person on the spot; here you have to leave the group, add the person elsewhere and come back.
Options: (a) keep it: groups are made from people you already have; (b) add "Add a new person" to the dialog, which creates the person and adds them to the group in one step. Recommendation: (b), it matches the other pickers. Default after 2026-11-25 04:45 UTC: wait; this is scope.

### The expired sign-in link page is light while the notebook is dark (look and feel)
An old sign-in link (`/login/<code>`) now shows a styled page with "Go to your notebook" (PR #1030). The page follows the browser's light or dark setting, so on a dark-themed notebook it shows a white card on pale grey (loop review of PR #1030).
Options: (a) keep following the browser's setting; (b) use the notebook's own theme (dark by default). Recommendation: (b), so it looks like part of the notebook. Default after 2026-11-25 04:45 UTC: wait; this is how the notebook looks.



### Where the "browser blocks site data" notice should sit (#1015 / PR #1035, look and feel)
When the browser blocks site data, the notebook shows a notice for about 12 s. PR #1035 already makes it closable (close button and Escape) and words it plainly. Placement is the only open point. At the top right it covers Chat with Godspeed and Add Moment. At the bottom it covers the chat's Add files, Dictate and Send buttons on a phone. Making it click-through lets a tap reach a button the person cannot see. Two send-backs, and the loop parked it.
Options: (a) an inline banner at the top of the page that pushes the content down, closable, with nothing covered; (b) keep a floating notice but shorter (about 5 s) and in a corner with no controls under it on each page; (c) another placement you name. Recommendation: (a). It covers nothing, and the person can read it at their own pace. Default after 2026-11-25 07:45 UTC: wait; this is how the notebook looks. Once you answer, one more lap builds it on PR #1035.
(Manager pass 2026-11-23 07:45 UTC. Between 05:37 and 06:41 UTC the on-call responder posted this same "owner pause" comment on PR #1035 thirteen times, about every 5 minutes. It has stopped since, but each round cost a run.)


### One more lap for PR #1028 (#988, Activity Log entries), over the send-back cap
PR #1028 makes one action write one Activity Log entry, and entries name their record. Its second review (05:17 UTC) confirmed the rename case is fixed. Two findings remain: (1) a regression, where an update that is not a rename, sent in its own request within 2 s of a create (a fact, a group membership), is folded into the Created entry and disappears from the log, while main logs it; (2) fact entries carry no name. Both have an exact fix written in the review. The loop parked it at the cap after three laps (e5d9b4e9 made no PR, then two send-backs). Narrowing would not help, since finding (1) is a regression the PR must not merge with.
Options: (a) one more lap on PR #1028 for exactly those two findings; (b) close #1028 and rebuild #988 from main later. Recommendation: (a). The rest of the PR passed review, and #967 and H-63..H-68 wait on it. Default after 2026-11-25 07:55 UTC: wait; the lap budget is yours.



### Asking the chat for today's brief on a morning with no brief saved yet (#1070, product behaviour)
Your beta.25 requirement says the chat stays ordinary chat when no brief was saved. Ticket 07 of beta.31 (#1039) makes the chat show the saved brief word for word when there is one. On a morning with none, the chat today writes its own ordinary answer, which reads like a brief that differs from the one the morning will save. One holdout scenario fails on main for this.
Options: (a) keep it ordinary chat (beta.25 as written); (b) make a brief on the spot and save it as today's brief; (c) say plainly that no brief was saved yet this morning, and offer to make one. Recommendation: (c): it keeps beta.25's rule of not inventing a brief and tells the person why. Default after 2026-11-25 10:45 UTC: wait; this is what a person gets.

### Should a moment carry a time of day? (#1059, scope)
Add and Edit Moment take a date only. The notebook itself stores and compares times (the write path accepts 2025-06-01T15:00:00Z), so a moment written by the assistant can carry a time the person can neither see nor correct in the form.
Options: (a) keep moments date-only in the forms; (b) add an optional time to Start and End (empty means all day), shown on the Timeline when set. Recommendation: (b). Default after 2026-11-25 10:45 UTC: wait; this is scope.

### Should other records carry a from-until date range? (#1060, scope)
Once PR #1038 (#1032) lands, a moment refuses an end before its start. No other record (person facts, World entries, media, goals, collection fields) has a from-until pair at all.
Options: (a) moments only, close #1060; (b) add a Date range field type to collections, with the same end-before-start refusal. Recommendation: (a) for now; (b) when a collection needs it. Default after 2026-11-25 10:45 UTC: wait; this is scope.

### One more lap each for two approved pull requests that now conflict with main (PR #1029 for #1017, PR #1038 for #1032)
Both were approved by the loop's review and refused only by the merge gate (its timing and "not what the app check tested" checks), so the dispatcher parked them at the cap. Main has since changed files they change, and both now conflict, so the manager cannot land them as it landed #992 this pass (checked against current main: whole notebook suite green, then merged at its reviewed head).
- PR #1029 (#1017, chat and search at phone and tablet widths): main changed `GlobalAIChatFAB.tsx` (#1036, #1063 is also in that file now). One holdout fails on main for this (the chat header cut to "Godspe…" once its counter has two digits).
- PR #1038 (#1032, a moment that ends before it starts): conflicts in the moment form. Four holdouts fail on main for this.
Options: (a) one lap each to merge main, re-run the app check and land at the tested head; (b) close them and rebuild from main. Recommendation: (a). Default after 2026-11-25 11:00 UTC: wait; the lap budget is yours.
